purpose: Teach: 変質/崇高/安堵/慰謝/感知/講ずる/発病/成就

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、戦時下に人格が変質した兵士の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, I remember your paper explored how soldiers' personalities shifted during wartime.
lines.style: Warm, curious, leaning slightly forward. Opens with his name like opening a door. Measured pace. The tone of a teacher who's genuinely interested in seeing where a student's mind went.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、宗教者の崇高な献身を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I focused on the religious figures' noble sense of commitment.
lines.style: Quiet, careful correction. Not defensive, but precise. A small pause before answering, as if making sure he's understood the question correctly. Steady eye contact.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、戦後の安堵感を表現した文学を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And your other work examined the literature that captured the relief people felt after the war ended.
lines.style: Thoughtful nod in the voice. Slower cadence, like walking through memory. Gentle acknowledgment of the weight of the subject. Not pushing, just reflecting back.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、被害者への慰謝料制度を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Actually, I wrote about the compensation systems that were created for victims.
lines.style: Soft clarification. A little hesitant — not contradicting so much as gently pointing to what he actually studied. The care of someone who doesn't want to be misunderstood but also doesn't want to seem ungrateful for the attention.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 感知できない放射線リスクを論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And the invisible dangers — the radiation risks people couldn't perceive — that was also in your research, wasn't it?
lines.style: Engaged but careful. Asking to confirm, not assert. Slight rise at the end like opening a conversation rather than closing one. Present, attentive.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、災害時の対策を講ずる行政手順を論文で扱いました
lines.en: That paper looked at how government systems developed emergency protocols during disasters.
lines.style: Steady correction, building on what came before. Not impatient. The tone of someone clarifying their own work without irritation. Clear, direct.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、戦時下の集団発病の歴史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: I also remember you examining the history of mass illness that emerged during wartime.
lines.style: Reflective, slightly slower. Genuine interest in the breadth of his research. A note of respect in the phrasing — recognizing the complexity of what he chose to study.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、社会運動が成就するまでの過程を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I explored how social movements developed and eventually came to fruition.
lines.style: Clear, complete answer. A sense of closure in the voice without rushing. Confident but not proud. The kind of steady response that marks the end of a good conversation.
